messages.author: c40d2469f7cdd6b5
messages.subject: Loading precomputed Plotly Plots.
parts:
I have saved a couple of plotly plots in a .RDS file and am reading it in on shiny. The system works perfectly fine locally, however, shinyio is throwing the following error:

 Warning: Error in normalizePath: path[1]="/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.3/Resources/library/plotly/htmlwidgets/lib/typedarray": No such file or directory

It looks like a problem with the plotly framework. I apologize if this is the wrong group to ask this question. Is this a permissions issue on shinyio? What could be causing this problem?

messages.author: 299a5089d6c6c523
messages.subject: Re: Loading precomputed Plotly Plots.
parts: Well, that path looks to be Mac specific, which indicates to me that the path is being stored in the RDS file, and when you attempt to load that on shinyapps.io, that path won't work because it is not your local computer.

messages.author: c40d2469f7cdd6b5
messages.subject: Re: Loading precomputed Plotly Plots.
parts: Found the solution. You were right, it seems like the creators of plotly or htmlwidgets are using absolute file paths for their dependencies. If "plot" is the name of the plot generated from plot_ly(), as an example, plot$dependancies[[1]]$src$file has a dependency defined by an absolute file path such as /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.3/Resources/library/plotly/htmlwidgets/lib/typedarray  on my mac. To make it work I changed this to /opt/R/3.3.2/lib/R/library/plotly/htmlwidgets/lib/typedarray a path on the shiny io server which works.
